conclusion: With 15 daily review slots across 139 held-out dates, event recall was 21.8% for the pending-sector rule and 9.8% for monitored fallback across 459 observable failures.

comparison.title: Failures warned before the event
comparison.note: Each drive and failure date counts once even with repeat warnings.

slice.title: Confirmed false alert episodes
slice.note: A consecutive episode with incomplete follow-up is reported as unresolved unless a failure is observed.

sensitivity.title: Lead time on detected failures
sensitivity.note: Lead time uses the earliest eligible warning in the fourteen-day horizon.

audit.monitor_window: Seven days of frozen-model alerts whose entire fourteen-day outcome window expired before today.

next_decision: Use the per-model alert counts, false investigations and warning time to set a review budget. Record whether missing measurements or delayed precision caused each fallback.

study_design.protocol: Keep the complete fleet's observation calendar. Train on earlier, disjoint serials and exclude one entire model. Evaluate fifteen daily alerts on unseen serials or the excluded model. Keep every observed candidate at allocation, then report unobservable follow-up separately; differentiate missing from zero. Compare a fixed pending-sector rule, a frozen empirical score and a fallback triggered by unavailable indicators or matured poor precision.

data.grain: One maximal consecutive run of equal binned SMART indicators for a pseudonymous drive
